report_name: CISA's 'A Tale of Two SOCs' Highlights Critical SOC Gaps

threat_actors.name: CISA Red Team
threat_actors.description: An authorized red team from the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) that conducted penetration testing exercises against two critical infrastructure organizations to assess their security monitoring and response capabilities.

attack_patterns.name: Default Accounts
attack_patterns.description: The CISA red team exploited default credentials on a public-facing web application to gain initial access to the government services entity.

attack_patterns.name: Internal Spearphishing
attack_patterns.description: After gaining initial access, the red team sent an internal phishing email to compromise four workstations within the government services entity's network.

attack_patterns.name: Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates
attack_patterns.description: Persistence was established by abusing misconfigured Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS) templates to create certificates, a technique noted as being similar to 'Certighost'.

attack_patterns.name: Credentials In Files
attack_patterns.description: The red team discovered cleartext credentials, including static Amazon Web Services (AWS) access keys, stored on file shares within the compromised network.

attack_patterns.name: Cloud Accounts
attack_patterns.description: Stolen static AWS access keys found on file shares were used to move laterally and access business-critical cloud resources.

attack_patterns.name: Pass the Hash
attack_patterns.description: Used for lateral movement within the compromised network, as identified in the report's pre-mapped techniques.

attack_patterns.name: Disable or Modify Tools
attack_patterns.description: The red team evaded detection by gaining access to the security team's email inbox to monitor for any signs of their activity being noticed.

tools.name: certutil
tools.description: The certutil.exe utility was noted as a potential tool for AD CS abuse, specifically for publishing certificates to Active Directory using the '-dspublish' command.

vulnerabilities.name: AD CS Misconfiguration
vulnerabilities.description: Misconfigured Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS) templates were abused by the CISA red team to establish persistence, a technique similar to 'Certighost'.

vulnerabilities.name: Default Credentials
vulnerabilities.description: Default credentials on a web application were exploited by the CISA red team to gain initial access to the government services entity.

vulnerabilities.name: Cleartext Credential Storage
vulnerabilities.description: Cleartext credentials and static AWS access keys were stored on file shares, allowing the red team to perform lateral movement to cloud resources.

identities.name: Government Services Entity (Organization A)
identities.description: A government services entity that was one of the targets of the CISA red team exercise. Its SOC failed to detect the intrusion due to alert fatigue, leading to a full domain compromise.

identities.name: Water Utility (Organization B)
identities.description: A water utility that was one of the targets of the CISA red team exercise. Its SOC successfully detected and neutralized the intrusion within an hour, demonstrating a mature defensive posture.

identities.name: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency
identities.description: The U.S. government agency that conducted the red team exercises and published the 'A Tale of Two SOCs' advisory (AA26-237A).

identities.name: Amazon Web Services
identities.description: Cloud service provider whose resources were accessed by the CISA red team using stolen static access keys found on the victim's file shares.

indicators.name: Suspicious DNSClient Policy Modification
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Suspicious DNSClient Policy Modification
id: 2b8a1c3d-4e5f-4a9b-8c7d-6e5f4a3b2c1d
status: experimental
description: Detects modification of the HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\DNSClient registry key, which could indicate attempts to manipulate DNS settings for redirection or C2 communication.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/cisa-red-team-compromised-two-critical.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-30
tags:
  - attack.t1562
level: medium
logsource:
  category: registry_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetObject|endswith: '\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\DNSClient'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects modification of a registry key related to DNS client policies, which was highlighted as an observable in the CISA red team report.

indicators.name: AD CS Certificate Publishing with Certutil
indicators.pattern:
title: AD CS Certificate Publishing with Certutil
id: f1d2c3b4-a5e6-4f9a-8b7c-6d5e4f3a2b1c
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of certutil.exe with the -dspublish flag to publish a certificate to Active Directory. This technique can be used to abuse AD CS for persistence or privilege escalation.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/cisa-red-team-compromised-two-critical.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-30
tags:
  - attack.t1649
  - attack.t1218
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\certutil.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' -dspublish '
      - '/dspublish '
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of `certutil.exe -dspublish`, a command line pattern identified in the CISA report related to AD CS abuse.
